<Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez>: On December 21, 2023, the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) issued a report\1\ finding that the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) procedures for reporting on Veteran-owned businesses need improvement.
\1\U.S. Gov't Accountability Off., GAO-24-106071, Small Business Administration: Procedures for Reporting on Veteran Owned Businesses Need Improvement (Dec. 21, 2023).
The SBA provides entrepreneurial training and education through Veterans Business Outreach Centers (VBOCs), mainly through the Boots to Business and Boots to Business Reboot programs. The SBA office responsible for overseeing the VBOC program is the Office of Veteran Business Development (OVBD). The Veterans Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development Act of 1999 requires the SBA to submit an annual report to the House and Senate Small Business and Veterans Affairs Committees on the needs of veteran-owned and service-disabled-veteran-owned businesses. This annual report must include information on: (1) the availability of SBA programs for such businesses and the degree of utilization by such businesses during the preceding 12-month period, including statistical information on such utilization compared to the small business community as a whole; (2) the percentage and dollar value of federal contracts awarded to such businesses during the preceding 12-month period; and (3) proposals to improve the access of such businesses to available assistance.\2\
\2\Veterans Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development Act of 1999 Sec.  603, 15 U.S.C. Sec.  657b note.
GAO found that the SBA's existing reporting and materials did not include the requisite information to satisfy the requirement.\3\ In response, the GAO issued a priority recommendation that the SBA establish policies and procedures to comply with the reporting requirement, to ensure it provides the Committee and others with information on the needs of veteran-owned small businesses. The SBA agreed with the recommendation.\4\
\3\U.S. Gov't Accountability Off., supra note 1.
\4\Id.
By developing procedures for ensuring compliance with reporting requirements, the SBA will have better information with which to serve veteran-owned small businesses. Unfortunately, this priority recommendation has not yet been closed out. As of September 8, 2026, SBA has 59 open GAO recommendations, 14 of which are priority recommendations.
Nydia M. Velazquez,
Ranking Member.
